bib.title: Evaluating Verifiability in Generative Search Engines

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Evaluating Verifiability in Generative Search Engines", Nelson F. Liu, Tianyi Zhang, Percy Liang (Stanford). arXiv:2304.09848v2 [cs.CL], 23 Oct 2023. Header and text read as an arXiv version with Limitations section (EMNLP-style Findings format); the extraction prints no venue, so treat as preprint unless you verify. Responses scraped late Feb to late Mar 2023.

COVERAGE: 74,394 of 74,394 chars read. That covers the main text, Limitations, references (skimmed), and Appendices A-H (queries, annotation guidelines and interface, agreement table, result tables). Annotation-guideline pages (Figs 8-12) extract as one word per line and were only skimmed. Figures 1-12 are images and were not viewed; I used their captions from the text.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Commercial generative search engines are fluent but often unverifiable. Averaged over all 4 systems, citation recall is 51.5% and citation precision is 74.5%.
  number: 51.5% / 74.5%
  setup: Human audit (Amazon Mechanical Turk, 34 annotators) of Bing Chat, NeevaAI, perplexity.ai and YouChat. 1450 queries per system, sentence-level statements, single-turn first response, Feb-Mar 2023.
  quote: "on average, a mere 51.5% of generated sentences are fully supported by citations and only 74.5% of citations support their associated sentence."
  where: abstract; Table 7/8 (chars ~68k+)
- Citation precision is inversely correlated with perceived utility across systems.
  number: r = -0.96
  setup: Correlation across the 4 systems (n=4 points, so weak evidence). Bing Chat has the highest precision (89.5) and lowest utility (4.34). YouChat has the lowest precision (63.6) and highest utility (4.62).
  quote: "citation precision is inversely correlated with perceived utility in existing generative search engines (r = −0.96)."
  where: §4.3
- The authors hypothesize that the inverse correlation arises because systems copy or closely paraphrase their cited pages. Copied text is supported by the source, but may not answer the query. The correlation is evidence, not a causal test.
  number: BLEU 31.3 and BERTScore F1 73.2 on average; r = 0.80 with precision. Bing Chat has BLEU 44.1 and BERTScore 78.8; perplexity.ai has 22.3 and 69.2.
  setup: Each generated statement is compared with the annotator-copied minimal evidence sentences from its cited page. For multiple citations, the maximum similarity is used. Only fully or partially supported citations are included.
  quote: "systems with higher similarity between their generated statements and cited webpages also have higher average citation precision (r = 0.80 between each of BLEU and BERTScore with average citation precision)"
  where: §4.4, Table 2
- Systems differ widely on recall and precision.
  number: Recall: perplexity.ai 68.7, NeevaAI 67.6, Bing Chat 58.7, YouChat 11.1. Precision: Bing Chat 89.5, perplexity.ai 72.7, NeevaAI 72.0, YouChat 63.6. Citation F1: Bing Chat 70.9, perplexity.ai 70.6, NeevaAI 69.8, YouChat 18.9.
  setup: Averaged over all 1450 queries. NeevaAI abstains on 22.7% of queries; the other three abstain on under 0.5%, which complicates comparison.
  quote: "perplexity.ai achieves the highest average recall (68.7), compared to NeevaAI (67.6), Bing Chat (58.7), and YouChat (11.1)."
  where: §4.2; Tables 1, 7-9
- Recall depends on whether retrieved pages directly answer the query. The authors hypothesize this; they did not test it.
  number: Recall is 58.5 for NaturalQuestions queries with a long answer vs 47.8 for the others. It is 63.4 with a short answer, 53.6 with only a long answer and 53.4 with no long answer. AllSouls essay questions score 44.3.
  setup: Pooled over the 4 systems.
  quote: "In the absence of retrieved evidence that directly answers the input user query, systems generate statements that are unsubstantiated by citations, resulting in lower recall."
  where: §4.2
- Precision is lowest on open-ended queries.
  number: AllSouls 67.8, davinci-debate 70.3. NaturalQuestions paragraph answers with a short answer score 81.5. The NaturalQuestions-with-long-answer average is 76.1 vs 72.3 for the others.
  setup: Pooled over the 4 systems.
  quote: "citation precision is lowest when systems are evaluated on AllSouls open-ended essay questions (67.8) and davinci-debate queries (70.3)."
  where: §4.2
- Fluency and perceived utility are high.
  number: Fluency 4.48 and perceived utility 4.50 on a 5-point Likert scale. Bing Chat scores 4.40/4.34 and YouChat 4.59/4.62.
  setup: Single annotator per pair, averaged over all systems and responses.
  quote: "Averaging across all systems and responses yields an average rating of 4.48 for fluency and 4.50 for perceived utility"
  where: §4.1
- Annotation agreement is high.
  number: Over 82.0% pairwise agreement and 91.0 F1.
  setup: 3 annotations on 250 random query-response pairs. The rest were annotated once.
  quote: "high agreement rates (greater than 82.0% pairwise agreement and 91.0 F1 for all judgments; see Appendix E)."
  where: §3.3; Table 4
- Metric definitions (useful for the note).
  number: Precision = (Tfs + Tps)/N. F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall.
  setup: Recall is the share of verification-worthy sentences fully supported by their citations. Precision is the share of citations that support their sentence. Partial citations count only if the union of the sentence's citations fully supports it and no single citation does. Support is judged with AIS (Rashkin et al. 2022): "According to cited webpages Ci, si".
  quote: "citation precision is (Tf s+ Tps)/N." Also: "a response that cites every webpage on the Internet for each generated statement would have high citation recall, but low citation precision"
  where: §2.3-2.5
- The authors argue every statement about the external world is verification-worthy. Annotators exclude only statements about the system itself and questions to the user.
  number: none
  quote: "We take the position that every generated statement about the external world is verification-worthy, even those that might seem obvious, trivially true, or “common sense”."
  where: §2.3

LIMITS
- The authors state that verifiability is not factuality. A supported statement may still be false, and an unsupported one may be true.
- Claims are scored at sentence level. Multi-claim sentences and the scope of a citation marker are ambiguous, and finer-grained evaluation is left to future work.
- Each pair was annotated once; agreement was measured on 250 pairs only.
- The audit covers 4 closed commercial systems in Feb-Mar 2023 and cannot see their retrieval or prompts. These systems have long since changed, so the numbers are dated.
- The 4 systems have different abstention rates (NeevaAI 22.7%) and different deployment contexts.
- The hypotheses (copying causes the precision/utility tradeoff; relevance of retrieval drives recall) are not tested with interventions.
- ChatGPT and Bard were excluded because they gave no inline citations.
- The citation checking is human annotation, not an automated metric.

CODE: none (no code in the paper). Annotations released at github.com/nelson-liu/evaluating-verifiability-in-generative-search-engines.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p1): James Webb example with per-citation full/partial/no support marks. It shows the recall and precision ideas fastest.
- Fig 2 (p3): worked recall/precision calculations, e.g. "Citation Recall: 3/3 = 100%, Citation Precision: 3/8 = 37.5%". It shows how partial citations are counted.
- Fig 3 (p6): perceived utility vs citation F1 per system.
- Fig 4 (p6): Bing Chat copying irrelevant cited text, giving high precision and low utility.
- Table 2 (BLEU/BERTScore) and Tables 7-9 hold the per-distribution results.
Figures were not viewed as images.
